77:1: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of God’s statement, And the winds sent forth in gusts. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: And the winds sent forth in gusts, one after the other. They said: And the winds sent forth are the winds. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, that he asked Ibn Mas’ud and he said: And the winds sent forth in gusts. He said: The wind. Khallad bin Aslam told us: Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us: Al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, that he asked Abdullah bin Masoud, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Hamid told me: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn, who said: I asked Abdullah ibn Masoud, and he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, and the winds sent forth in gusts, meaning the wind. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Ubaid bin Muadh told us: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, the companion of Al-Kalbi, regarding his statement, And the winds sent forth in gusts, he said: They are the winds. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the winds sent forth in gusts. He said: The wind. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, who said: I asked Abdullah about those sent forth in a gusty wind. He said: The wind. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And the winds sent forth in gusts, he said: It is the wind. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: and the angels who are sent with custom. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, who said: Masruq used to say about the messengers: They are the angels. Israel bin Abi Israel told us, he said: Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us, he said: Shuba told us, on the authority of Sulayman, he said: I heard Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding his statement, And the angels sent forth in gusts, he said: The angels. Abu Kurayb told us: Jabir bin Nuh and Wakee’ told us on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, And the messengers sent forth in gusts, he said: They are the messengers sent forth in gusts. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Sakari told us: Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail, who said: I asked Abu Saleh about his statement, And the messengers sent forth in kindness. He said: They are the messengers sent forth in kindness. They said: So the interpretation of the statement is the angels who were sent forth with the command and prohibition of God, and that is kindness. Some of them said: What he meant by his saying according to the mane of a horse is that it was successive, like the mane of a horse, as the Arabs said: People are heading towards so-and-so as one mane, if they head towards him in large numbers. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Salih ibn Buraidah, regarding his statement, They are known, he said: They follow one another. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that God, the Most High, swore by the messengers sent by custom. The angels are sent by custom, and the winds are sent likewise. There is no evidence that indicates that what is meant by this is one of the two parties rather than the other. God, the Most High, has made His oaths general, including everything that has the description I have described. So everyone whose description is like this, then included in His oath is an angel, a wind, or a messenger from the children of Adam who is sent.
77:2: And His saying: And the violently stormy winds, God Almighty says: The violently stormy winds, meaning the ones that blow violently and pass quickly. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Arara, that a man stood up to Ali, may God be pleased with him, and said: What are the violent storms? He said: The wind. Khallad bin Aslam told us: Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us: Al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, on the authority of Abdullah, the same. Abu Kurayb told us: Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, that he asked Abdullah bin Mas’ud, saying: What are the violent storms? He said: The wind. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn, who said: I asked Abdullah, and he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: And the violent storms he said: The wind. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Kuraib narrated to us: Jabir bin Nuh narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih: And the violent storms he said: They are the winds. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us: Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail, who said: I asked Abu Saleh about his statement, And the violent storms. He said: They are the winds. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abdullah bin Muadh told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, the companion of Al-Kalbi, regarding his statement, And the violent storms, he said: They are the winds. Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari told us: Abu Muawiyah Al-Dharee’ and Saeed bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh, regarding his statement, And the violent storms, he said: It is the wind. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh, the same. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, And the violent storms he said: The wind. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And the violent storms, he said: the winds. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same.
77:3: And his saying: And the spreaders spreading. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: What is meant by the spreaders spreading is the wind. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, that he asked Ibn Mas’ud about the winds that spread. He said: The wind. Khallad bin Aslam told us: Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us: Al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn, who said: I asked Abdullah ibn Masoud, and he mentioned something similar. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn, who said: I asked Abdullah, and he mentioned something similar. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And the spreaders spreading he said: The wind. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ubayd God bin Muadh told us: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, the companion of Al-Kalbi, regarding His statement, And the spreaders spreading, he said: They are the winds. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the spreaders spreading he said: the winds. Others said: It is rain. Who said that? Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us: Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail, who said: I asked Abu Saleh about his statement, And the spreaders spreading out. He said: The rain. Abu Kurayb told us: Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, And the spreaders spreading he said: It is the rain. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh, the same. Others said: Rather, they are the angels who spread the books. Who said that? Ahmad bin Hisham told us: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Saleh, And the spreaders spreading out he said: The angels spread out the books. The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is to say: God Almighty swore by the things that spread out, and He did not specify one of them over another. So the winds spread out the clouds, the rain spreads out the earth, and the angels spread out the books. There is no indication from any source that must be accepted that what is meant by this is some and not others, so that applies to everything that spreads.
77:4: And his saying: And the distinguishing ones are the distinguishing ones. The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: What he meant by that is: the angels who distinguish between truth and falsehood. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih: Then the distinguishing ones are the angels. He said: The angels. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh, Then the distinguishing ones are the distinguishing ones. He said: The angels. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Ismail, the same. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the distinguishing ones he said: The angels. Others said: Rather, he meant the Qur’an. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The distinguishing verses means the Qur’an in which God distinguished between truth and falsehood. The correct thing to say about this is: Our Lord, may His praise be glorified, swore by the distinguishing features: which are the separators between truth and falsehood. He did not specify some of them over others. So this is an oath by every distinguisher between truth and falsehood, whether it is an angel, the Qur’an, or something else.
77:5: And his saying: And those who convey the message means: Those who convey the revelation of God to His Messenger, and they are the angels. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And those who cast down the Reminder meaning: the angels. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And those who convey the Reminder, he said: They are the angels who convey the Reminder to the Messengers and deliver it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And those who recite the Reminder He said: The angels recite the Qur’an. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, And those who bring forth remembrance, he said: The angels.
77:6: And His saying: An excuse or a warning, God Almighty says: So the messages sent to the messengers are an excuse from God to His creation, and a warning from Him to them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: An excuse or a vow. He said: An excuse from God, and a vow from Him to His creation. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, an excuse or a vow: God’s excuse for His creation, and a vow for the believers, from which they may benefit and take it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, An excuse or a vow meaning: the angels. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Ash-Sham, some of the Meccans, and some of the Kufians recited it as adhran with a light pronunciation, or nadhri with a heavy pronunciation. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the Basrans recited it with a light pronunciation, and others from Basra recited it with a heavy pronunciation. The light pronunciation in both of them is more pleasing to me, even though I do not deny the validity of the heavy pronunciation, because they are two sources meaning excuse and warning.
77:7: God Almighty says: By the messengers sent forth in succession. Indeed, what you are promised, O people, of matters will surely happen, and it will inevitably occur. By that, He means the Day of Resurrection, and what God mentioned that He has prepared for His creation on that day of reward and punishment.
77:8: And his saying: Then the stars will be extinguished means: Then the stars will have lost their light, and they will have no light or radiance.
77:9: And the Almighty said: And when the sky is split open meaning: And when the sky is split open and cracked.
77:10: God Almighty says: And when the mountains are blown away. He says: And when the mountains are blown away from their origin, and become scattered dust.
77:11: God Almighty says: And when the messengers are gathered together God Almighty says: And when the messengers are put off to meet at their appointed time on the Day of Resurrection. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And when the messengers gather, he said: they gathered. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, I have set a deadline, he said: I have postponed. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: Mujahid said: And when the messengers are given a meal, he said: they are given a meal. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki` told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us both, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, And when the messengers are threatened, he said: They are threatened. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And when the messengers are gathered together, he said: They are gathered together for the Day of Resurrection. And he recited, The Day when God will gather the messengers (al-Ma’idah 5:109). He said: And the appointed time is the appointed time. And he recited, “They ask you about the new moons. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for mankind and for Hajj’” (al-Baqarah 2:189). And he recited, Until the appointed time of a known day (al-Waqi’ah 56:50), until the Day of Resurrection. He said: They have an appointed time until that day so that they may reach it. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, And when the messengers are promised, he said: They are promised. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina, except Abu Ja`far, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as aqtat with an alif and a shaddah on the qaf. Some of the reciters of Basra read it with a waw and a shaddah on the qaf waqat. Abu Ja`far read it as waqat with a waw and a soft qaf. The correct thing to say about this is that all of these are well-known readings and famous languages with one meaning, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. It is a verb from the word fa’ala i.e., at-taqwat, except that some Arabs find the damma of the waw heavy, just as they find the kasra of the ya’ at the beginning of the letter heavy, so they pronounce it with a hamza and say: This is ajwa hassan with a hamza. Some of them recite: It is solved by one of them and it is said that it is a husband and a proverb that means poverty
77:12: And His statement: For what day have you postponed? The Most High says, astonishing His servants with the terror and severity of that day. For what day have the messengers been postponed and timed? How great and terrifying it is. Then He explains: And what day is it? He says: For the Day of Judgment. He says: The day on which God will judge between His creation, and He will take for the oppressed from the oppressor, and He will reward the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: For what day have you been appointed? For the Day of Judgment. The day on which people will be judged by their deeds, to Paradise or to Hell.
77:13: God Almighty says: On the Day of Judgment.
77:14: And His saying: And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And what will make you know, O Muhammad, what the Day of Judgment is, thereby magnifying its matter and the severity of its terror. As Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is? as a sign of the greatness of that day.
77:15: And His saying: Woe on that Day to the deniers. God Almighty says: The valley in which the pus of its people flows in Hell is for those who deny the Day of Judgment. God Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. Woe, by God, is long.
77:16: God Almighty says: Did We not destroy the past nations who denied My messengers and rejected My signs, from the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud, and then We made others follow them after them, who followed their path in disbelief in Me and My messenger, like the people of Abraham, the people of Lot, and the people of Madyan, so We destroyed them as We destroyed the former peoples before them.
77:17: God Almighty says: Then We will make others follow them.
77:18: God Almighty says: Thus do We deal with the criminals. He says, just as We destroyed these people for their disbelief in Me and their denial of My messengers, so is My way with the likes of them from the disbelieving nations. We destroy the criminals for their crimes when they transgress and rebel.
77:19: God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to those who deny the report of God that we mentioned in this verse, those who deny His ability to do whatever He wills.
77:20: God Almighty says: Did We not create you, O people, from a despised water? meaning from a weak sperm. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Did We not create you from a despised water? He means by despised: weak.
77:21: And His statement: So We placed it in a secure lodging, meaning: So We placed the despised water in a womb in which it settled and became established. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, in a secure place, he said: the womb.
77:22: And his saying: to a known measure means: to a known time for his exit from the womb with God, So We have measured, and excellent are the measurers The reciters differed in the reading of that, so the majority of the reciters of Medina read it So We have measured with emphasis, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it with emphasis. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. However, I prefer to make it lighter, because of his saying, Then excellent are the Able Ones, since the Arabs combined the two languages, as he said, So give the disbelievers respite, give them respite for a while (Al-Tariq: 17). So he combined the emphasis and the lightening, as Al-A’sha said: You denied me, but the only thing you denied of the incidents was my bald gray hair. It is possible that the meaning is the same in both emphasis and relaxation, as it is reported from the Arabs: death was decreed for him, and it was decreed with emphasis and relaxation.
77:23: What he meant by his saying: So We have decreed, and indeed We are able, is what Ibn Hamid told us. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak: So We have decreed, and indeed We are able. He said: So We have control, and indeed We are able.
77:24: And His saying: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers that God created them from despised water.
77:25: God Almighty says, reminding His servants of His blessings upon them: Have We not made, O people, the earth a receptacle for you? He says: a container. You say: This receptacle is this and I receptacle for it, if it is its receptacle. The meaning of the words is: Have We not made the earth a receptacle for your living and your dead, to suffice your living in the dwellings and houses, to contain them in it and gather them, and your dead in its bellies in the graves, so they are buried in it. It is possible that what he meant by his saying Sufficient for the living and the dead is that he sufficed for their harm while they were alive, and their corpses after their death. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Have We not made the earth a receptacle? He said: We were. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us: Khalid told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Zadan Abu Omar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, that he found a louse on his garment, so he buried it in the mosque and then said: Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead? Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us, he said: Muslim Al-Awar told us, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Rabi’ bin Khaitham, on the authority of Abdullah, the same. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, he said: Mujahid said about the one who sees a louse on his garment, while he is in the mosque, and I do not know whether he said during prayer or not: If you wish, throw it away, and if you wish, bury it. Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Bayan, on the authority of Al-Sha`bi: Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead? He said: Its belly is for your dead, and its back is for your living. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid: Have We not made the earth a receptacle? He said: It receptacles their harm. Alive conceals it. And dead they are buried: it receptacles them. Ibn Hamid told me about it another time, saying: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid: Have We not made the earth a receptacle? He said: It receptacles their harm and what comes out of them. The living and the dead. He said: It receptacles them among the living and the dead. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Have We not made the earth a receptacle * for the living and the dead? He said: Alive and existing in it. Muhammad ibn Amr said: They disappear in it as they wish. Al-Harith said: And they disappear in it as they wish.
77:26: And his saying: Alive and dead, he said: They are buried in it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead? Their living will live in it and their dead will be buried in it. Hadith of Ibn Abd al-A’la, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, The living and the dead. He said: The living above it on its surface, and the dead who are buried in it. The Arabists differed about who put the word living and dead in the accusative case. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is in the accusative case as a state. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Rather, it is in the accusative case because the two hands fall on it, as if you said: Have We not made the earth a handkerchief for the living and the dead? Then if you add a nun, it is in the accusative case, as someone who reads: Or feeding on a day of famine * An orphan near of kin (al-Balad 90:14-15). This statement seems more correct to me.
77:27: And His statement: And We placed therein firm, lofty mountains. God Almighty says: And We placed on the earth firm mountains, lofty and towering. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We placed therein lofty mountains, meaning the mountains. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, lofty mountains, meaning: lofty mountains. His saying: And We gave you fresh water to drink means: And We gave you sweet water to drink. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We gave you fresh water to drink, meaning: sweet. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told me, he said: Isa told me, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, fresh water, he said: sweet. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We gave you fresh water to drink: meaning sweet water. Muhammad bin Sinan al-Qazzaz told us: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We gave you to drink sweet water. He said: From four rivers: the Seyhan, the Ceyhan, the Nile, and the Euphrates. Every water that the son of Adam drinks is from these rivers, and they flow from under a rock near Jerusalem. As for the Seyhan, it reaches, as for the Ceyhan, it is the Tigris, as for the Euphrates, it is the Euphrates of Kufa, and as for the Nile, it is in Egypt.
77:28: And His statement: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. He says: Woe, that Day, to those who deny these blessings that I have bestowed upon you from My creation and who disbelieve in them.
77:29: God Almighty says to those who deny these blessings and the arguments that He will use against them on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Go to what you used to deny in this world, of God’s punishment for those who disbelieved in Him.
77:30: God Almighty said: Go to a shade of three branches. God Almighty means: to a shade of smoke with three branches not shade. This is because smoke rises from its fuel, as mentioned, and when it rises, it splits into three branches. This is what He said: with three branches. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, to a shade of three branches, he said: the smoke of Hell. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, A shade with three branches. He said: It is like His saying, A fire whose curtain will surround them. (al-Kahf 18:29) He said: The curtain is the smoke of the fire, and its curtain will surround them, then it will disperse and become three branches. Then He said: Go to a shade with three branches: a branch here, a branch there, and a branch there. No shade, nor will it protect against the flame.
77:31: And God Almighty said: There is no shade nor does it protect against the flame. His saying: No shade means: It neither shades them from its heat, nor protects them from the flame nor protects them from its flame.
77:32: And His saying: It throws out sparks like palaces. God Almighty says: Hell throws out sparks like palaces. The reciters of the regions read it as like palaces with the sad pronounced with a jazm. Those who read it also differed about its meaning. Some of them said: It is one of the palaces. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, It throws out sparks like castles, meaning: like a huge castle. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: It throws sparks like palaces. He said: He mentioned palaces. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yazid ibn Yunus told me, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, regarding the statement of God, It throws out sparks like castles, he said: Al-Qurazi used to say: Hell has a wall, and what comes out from behind the wall of what returns to it is the size of castles and the color of tar. Others said: Rather, it is the thick wood, like the roots of palm trees and the like. Who said that? Waki` narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about his statement, It throws out sparks like castles. He said: The castle is wood that we used to store for the winter, three cubits long, and above that, and less than that, we used to call it the castle. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abbas, he said: I heard Ibn Abbas say regarding His statement, It throws out sparks like castles, he said: Castles are wood that was cut in the pre-Islamic era, a cubit or less or more, and used as a pillar. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abbas, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say regarding His statement, It throws out sparks like castles. He said: In the pre-Islamic era, we used to shorten the distance to two or three cubits, and what was above that and less than that we called it a castle. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, It throws out sparks like castles. Castles are the cut-down trees, and it is also said: the cut-down palm trees. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, like a palace, he said: the bundles of trees, meaning the bundle. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Ibn Abi `Uday told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: It throws out sparks like palaces. He said: Like the palaces of palm trees. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, It throws out sparks like palaces, means the roots of trees and the roots of palm trees. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: With sparks like palaces. He said: Like the roots of trees. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, with sparks like castles, the castles are the roots of large trees, as if they were camel saddlebags in the middle of everything, and they are the saddlebags. Ahmad bin Yusuf told us: Al-Qasim told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, who said: Al-Hasan read it as like a palace, and he said it is a large piece of wood. He said: Its singular is qasra and qasr, like it: jamrah and jamr, and tamrah and tamar. It was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he read it as like the palace with a moving sad. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, he said: Husayn al-Mu’allim told me, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he read it like the palace with the qaf and the sad open. He said: And Harun said: Abu Amr told me that Ibn Abbas read it as like the palace and said: The palace of the palm trees, meaning the necks. The first of the two readings that is more correct in our view is what the reciters of the regions do, which is the sukoon on the sad, and the first interpretation of it is that it is a palace from palaces, and that is because his saying as if it were a yellow camel indicates its correctness, and the Arabs liken camels to built palaces, as Al-Akhtal said in describing a female camel: It is like a Roman tower built with plaster, bricks and stones. It was said: With sparks like palaces, and he did not say like palaces, and sparks are a group, as it was said: Then the group will be defeated and they will turn their backs (al-Qamar 54:45), and he did not say their backs, because their backs means their backs, and he did that to reconcile the beginnings of the verses and the endings of the speech, because the Arabs do that likewise, and the Qur’an was revealed in their language. It was said: Like a palace, and the meaning of the speech is: like the size of a palace, as it was said: Their eyes will roll like one who faints from death (al-Ahzab 33:19), and he did not say: like the eyes of one who faints, because what is meant in the simile is the action, not the eye. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Ata` ibn al-Sa`ib, that he asked al-Aswad about this verse: It throws sparks like palaces. He said: Like palaces.
77:33: And his saying: yellow camels The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that, some of them said: The meaning of that is, as if the sparks that Hellfire throws are like palaces. Black camels: that is, very black. And they said: Yellow in this place means black. They said: And it was called yellow and it is black, because the colors of camels tend toward yellow, and for that reason it was called yellow, just as gazelles were called red, because of the darkness that rises above them in their whiteness. Who said that? Ahmad bin Amr Al-Basri told me, he said: Badal bin Al-Muhber told us, he said: Ibad bin Rashid told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Hasan as if they were yellow camels, he said: The black ones. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada as if they were yellow camels like the black camels that you saw. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement yellow camels, he said: black camels. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, and Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid as if they were yellow camels, he said: They are camels. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada as if they were yellow camels he said: like the black camels that you saw. Others said: Rather, he meant the ships’ sails, likening them to sparks. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saeed told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas as if they were yellow camels. The yellow camels are the ships’ saddles that are gathered together and used to secure the ships. Abu Kuraib told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about his statement, As if they were yellow camels. He said: The ships of the sea are mounted on top of each other, until they are like the middle of men. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abbas, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas asked about yellow camels. He said: They are the ropes of ships, some of which are tied together until they are like the waists of men. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abbas, he said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abdullah told us, he said: Hilal ibn Khabab told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement yellow camels, he said: The camels of the bridge. Muhammad bin Huwaira bin Muhammad Al-Manqari told me, he said: Abdul Malik bin Abdullah Al-Qattan told us, he said: Hilal bin Khabab told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the same. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and Ibn Abi `Uday told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr as if they were yellow camels, he said: the ropes. Abu Kuraib told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas as if they were yellow camels, he said: The ships of the sea. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement as if they were yellow camels he said: the ropes of bridges. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: as if he cut copper. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement as if they were yellow camels means: pieces of copper. The first of the sayings that is most correct in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by yellow camels is black camels, because that is what is known from the speech of the Arabs, and that camels is the plural of camel, like men and men, and houses and houses. The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as jamalat with a kasra on the jim and the ta’ as if it means camels. It may also be possible that what is meant by it is the plural of jamalah, and jamalah is the plural of camel, just as hujra is the plural of hujr, and dhikr is the plural of dhikr. The majority of the Kufian reciters read it as ka’anhu jamalah with a kasra on the jim as if it is the plural of jamal, the plural of jamalah, just as I mentioned about the plural of hujr being hujra. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to read jamalat with a ta’ and a damma on the jim as if it was the plural of jamalah from something that is general. Ahmad bin Yusuf told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Al-Hussein Al-Mu’allim, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The correct thing to say about this is that the reader can choose whichever of the two readings he wants, from breaking the jīm and reading it with a ta’, or breaking the jīm and reading it with a ha’ which becomes a ta’ in connection, because these are the two readings known among the reciters of the regions. As for adding a damma to the jīm, I do not permit it due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters to the contrary.
77:34: And His statement: Woe on that Day to the deniers. God Almighty says: Woe on the Day of Resurrection to the deniers. This is the threat with which God has threatened the deniers among His servants.
77:35: God Almighty says to those who deny God’s reward and punishment: This is a Day when they will not speak those who deny God’s reward and punishment will not be permitted to apologize for the sins they committed in this world. If someone were to say: How can it be said, This is a Day when they will not speak, when you know from God’s report about them that they will say, Our Lord, bring us out of it (Al-Mu’minun 33:107), and that they will say, Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice (Ghafir 30:11), in similar instances of what God and His Messenger reported about them saying? It will be said: That is in some cases and not in others. His saying: This is a day on which they will not speak indicates that they will not speak during some of the circumstances of that day, not that they will not speak that entire day. If he says: Is there a proof by which the reality of that is known? It is said: Yes, and that is by adding day to His statement they do not speak. The Arabs do not add day to the verb yaf’ala except if they mean the hour of the day or the time of it, such as when they say: I will come to you on the day so-and-so arrives, and I came to you on the day your brother visited you. So it is known that the meaning of that is: I came to you at the hour he visited you, or I will come to you at the hour he arrives, and that his coming to him did not take the whole day, because if that had taken the whole day, then day would not have been added to the verb yaf’ala and yaf’ala. But he did that because day means when and when, which are verbs and not nouns.
77:36: And his saying: and they excuse themselves is in the nominative case in apposition to his saying: and they are not permitted to do so. This was chosen over the accusative case, and before it was a denial, because it is the beginning of a verse that was linked to the rest of the beginnings of the verses that preceded it. If it had come in the accusative case, it would have been permissible, as he said: It is not decreed that they die. And all of that is permissible with it, I mean the nominative and the accusative case, as it was said: Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him? (al-Baqarah 2:245), in the nominative and the accusative case.
77:37: And His statement: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to those who deny God’s report about these people, and what He will do to them on the Day of Resurrection.
77:38: And His statement: “This is the Day of Judgment. We will gather you and the former peoples.” God Almighty says to those who deny the Resurrection on the Day they are resurrected: This is the Day of Judgment on which God will judge between His servants in truth. We will gather you and the former peoples. He says: We will gather you on it for the appointment that We promised you in this world, the gathering on it between you and all the nations that came before you, the destroyed ones. We have fulfilled that for you.
77:39: God Almighty says: If you have a plan, then plan. He says: God will fulfill for you what He promised you in this world of punishment for your denial of Him, that you will be resurrected on this day. If you have a plan to devise to escape His punishment today, then plan.
77:40: And His saying: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. He says, Woe, that Day, to the deniers of this report.
77:41: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who feared God’s punishment by performing His obligations in this world and avoiding His sins will be in shade shady, and shelter, neither heat nor cold will harm them, while the disbelievers in God will be in shade with three branches, neither shade nor protection from the flame. And springs that flow through the trees of their gardens.
77:42: And His saying: And fruits of whatever they desire means that they eat from it whenever they desire, without fearing its harm or any unpleasant consequences.
77:43: And His statement: Eat and drink in pleasure for what you used to do. God Almighty says: It will be said to them: Eat, O people, from these fruits, and drink from these springs whenever you desire in pleasure. He says: There will be no disturbance to you, nor will there be any annoyance in what you eat and drink from it, but it is for you permanently, it does not go away, and it is pleasant, and it will not cause you any harm in your bodies. And His saying: For what you used to do, He, the Most High, says that it will be said to them: This is a reward for what you used to do in this world in obedience to God, and for striving to do that which brings you closer to Him.
77:44: And His statement: Thus do We reward the doers of good. He says: Just as We rewarded these righteous people with the reward We described for their obedience to Us in this world, thus We reward and recompense the people of goodness for their obedience to Us and their worship of Us in this world for their goodness. We do not waste their reward in the Hereafter.
77:45: And His statement: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. He says: Woe to those who deny God’s report of what He told them about His honoring these righteous people with what He honored them with on the Day of Resurrection.
77:46: God Almighty says, threatening and warning those who deny the al-Qiyamah 75:Eat during the remainder of your terms, and enjoy the remainder of your lives. You are criminals. You are being subjected to the same practice of the criminal nations before you, who enjoyed their lives until their written terms reached their appointed times, then God took revenge on them for their disbelief and denial of their messengers. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Eat and enjoy yourselves a little, for indeed, you are criminals, he said: He meant the people of disbelief.
77:47: And His statement: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers who denied the report of God that He informed them of about what He would do to them in this verse.
77:48: And His statement: And when it is said to them, ‘Bow down,’ they do not bow down. God Almighty says: And when it is said to these criminals who deny God’s threat, the people who deny it, ‘Bow down,’ they do not bow down. The commentators differed about the time when it will be said to them. Some of them said: It will be said in the Hereafter when they are called to prostrate but they are unable to. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when it is said to them, ‘Bow down,’ they do not bow down, meaning: They will be called on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate, but they will not be able to prostrate because they did not prostrate to God in this world. Others said: Rather, that was said to them in this world. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Qatada told us, his statement, And when it is said to them, ‘Bow down,’ they do not bow down, you must bow properly, for prayer has a place with God. Qatada said on the authority of Ibn Masoud: He saw a man whose prayer God accepted, but as for the Hereafter, God does not look at him. It was said: What is meant by bowing in this place is prayer. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And when it is said to them, ‘Bow down,’ they do not bow down, he said: Pray. The first statement on this matter is that it is report from God Almighty about these criminal people, that they were disobedient to Him in His commands and prohibitions, they did not obey His commands, and they did not refrain from what He forbade them from.
77:49: And His statement: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. He says: Woe to those who denied the Messengers of God, and rejected what they had conveyed to them of God’s command to them and His prohibition to them.
77:50: God Almighty says: So in what statement after this Qur’an, that is, you, O people, have denied it despite the clarity of its proof and the soundness of its evidence, that it is the truth from God, do you believe? He says: You believe. Rather, the Most High informed them that if they did not believe in this report that He informed them of in this Qur’an, despite the soundness of His proofs for its truth, they would not be able to acknowledge the truth of any of the report that they did not see the one being informed about, nor did they witness it. And if they believed in something that was hidden from them, the evidence for it would be established for them, and the same would be required of them in the report of this Qur’an. And God knows best.
